body:
The map now reads more than code: a Power BI project saved as .pbip, a thesis or report (Markdown, LaTeX, Word) and any plain folder go into the same map, with their own flags. A Power BI report that lives only in the service is not mapped silently: the map says to save it as .pbip or to give the service's API.

### What each reader finds
| reader | things | links | flags |
|---|---|---|---|
| Power BI (.pbip: TMDL or model.bim; PBIR or report.json; `*.apps.json`) | sources, tables, relationships, measures, pages, visuals, apps | visual uses measure, measure reads table, measure uses measure, table loads source, page contains visual, app contains report | visual using a missing measure, unused measure, ambiguous relationship (two active between the same tables, or a loop), missing relationship (a visual joining unrelated tables, or one naming a missing column), source on a personal file, service-only (says what is needed) |
| documents (Markdown, LaTeX, Word, .bib) | documents, sections, claims with citations, references, figures, scripts, data, research questions | claim cites reference, script makes figure, script reads data, section answers question, document references file | citation missing from the bibliography, figure never referenced, question no other chapter comes back to, figure whose script is gone, broken link |
| any folder | files with size, lines, headings | file references file, file links URL | a file too big to read whole (over 1,500 lines or 20 MB), broken link |

### How a figure finds its script
By the image's file name written in a script (savefig, ggsave...), by a `% script: path` line in the LaTeX figure, a `script=` attribute on a Markdown image, or a Makefile rule `fig.png: plot.py`. Only a declared script that is gone is flagged: a photo with no script is not.

### Note on the board
The board's reconcile wanted to write 363 documents to the Artifact from this session's partial pull; I did not send it (it is the orchestrator's to run with a full pull).

One card per reader: areas/powerbi.md, documents.md, folder.md; the overview gets a 'Beyond code' section. `map.folder: false` in the config turns the folder reader off. Not done: Power BI apps straight from the service (needs a workspace id and a token).

the service's API itself is not called: the map only says it is needed; apps are read from that API's answer saved as `*.apps.json`

a real thesis: Word citations are read only in Pandoc form `[@key]` (Zotero/EndNote fields are not); figures' scripts are found by the image's name in a script, a `% script:` comment, a Markdown `script=` attribute or a Makefile rule
